title: Microsoft Teams' aggressive bundling and bloated UI is sparking a massive 'lean-and-agile' migration trend among SMBs
description: As Microsoft Teams continues to balloon in both cost and complexity, small-to-medium businesses (SMBs) and agile units are aggressively seeking lightweight chat alternatives. Teams is universally hated for its clunky UI, poor notification handling, heavy resource consumption, and forcing companies to pay for an entire suite of enterprise bloatware they never use. The pain of navigating a 2GB RAM-hogging app just to send a text message has reached a breaking point.
the_opportunity: Build a hyper-fast, low-RAM, 'developer-first' group chat application that competes directly against the bloat of Teams and Slack. Cut out video conferencing, complex thread nesting, and corporate app integrations. Deliver a pure, blazing-fast text protocol with robust search, Markdown support, and native API webhooks. Target engineering and startup teams looking to cut subscription overhead by 70-80% while retaining mission-critical communication speed.
the_gap: The 'enterprise chat' market has been completely taken over by Slack and Teams, both of which have evolved into massive, sluggish operating systems. The gap is the lack of a modern 'IRC for the 2020s',a dedicated, lightweight tool that doesn't hold your CPU hostage and respects the user's attention.

sample_quotes.text: Honestly these tools feel like they were designed by people who never worked in a real team. Using Teams is like trying to drive a tank to the grocery store. It takes 15 seconds just to load a chat history.
sample_quotes.author: @Brady-b5w4w

sample_quotes.text: You now have to pay... and the price will double after your first 3 months... And you will be forced to increase your on-line storage. Whatever happened to 'do no evil'?
sample_quotes.author: @KitPeters001

sample_quotes.text: My laptop fans spin up every time someone sends a GIF in the general channel. We are paying $20,000 a year for a chat app that actively slows down our engineers.
sample_quotes.author: Reddit CTO
